source_acquisition.search_note: The automated inventory row was no_public_source_found and corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-c6856f20a2f5/ is absent. The author-linked GitHub repository https://github.com/eth-sri/robust-llm-fingerprints was checked with gh (main); its README/tree contain fingerprint, watermark, evaluation and stealth-judge implementation but no matching plot, figure, table, notebook, SVG or TeX visual generator. The arXiv source package for 2505.16723 was then acquired from the paper identity: 00README.json specifies pdflatex/TeX Live 2025, and its exact figure PDF assets, figure wrappers/captions and Table 1–9 LaTeX sources cover every numbered PDF object. The final status is exact_visual_source for the paper-side assets/inclusions; no original plotting/data generator was found, so unencoded colors, sizes and line widths remain rendered estimates. OpenReview API returned a challenge/403 and was not used as visual evidence; local visual-source directory was not present.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Teal/coral/slate identify Ours/IF/Scalable in the stealth bars; blue/orange/green/red/purple identify domains or perturbations in line/ROC plots, with a red dashed α=1e−3 threshold and gray y=α identity where applicable. Pale green/pink cells encode FSR success/failure and pale blue marks the French benchmark. Color carries major semantics in most curves and matrices, while Figure 6 and tables add line/marker or text structure.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The official PDF and the arXiv assets are vector/text dominated: chart lines, axes, legends, table rules and captions remain vector at 200 dpi. Figure 1 includes embedded icon/image resources and Type3 figure text, so the complete set is mixed; no page was treated as a full-page raster. Appendix G cards were inspected separately and are unnumbered qualitative examples.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math stabilize body/caption/table typography; DejaVu Sans and ArialMT appear inside figure assets, with Bera Sans Mono in qualitative cards. One-column 5.5-inch layout is consistent, while large robustness matrices use resizebox and compressed type. Bold caption titles and booktabs rules are stable through Table 8; Figures 10–12 use shorter non-bold captions and lower explanatory redundancy.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Illustration of Model Fingerprinting Left: The model owner trains and releases a model in which they have previously embedded a fingerprint. A malicious deployer modifies the model and deploys it behind an API without honoring its restrictive license. Right: In prior work, fingerprint detection relies on specific query-key pairs, which are neither stealthy nor robust to most deployment scenarios. We propose to use semantic domains (e.g., French) and statistical signals (e.g., semantically conditioned LLM watermarks), making the fingerprint stealthy and consistently detectable.

color.semantic_mapping: gray/black threat lane; orange prior query-key lane; blue/green ours semantic-domain/statistical-signal lane; red X and green check encode failure/success.

encodings.x: 从 owner training 经 API deployment 到 prior works/ours 的左至右阶段顺序
encodings.y: 各 lane 内的训练、攻击、query/reply 和结论层级

encodings.shape: 机器人、API、prompt/reply、check/X、法国旗和水滴图标
encodings.line: 箭头、虚线框、lane 分隔线与上下等号
encodings.facet: Threat Model / Prior works / Ours 三个 lane
encodings.text: 阶段标签、Query-Key brittle、Semantic Domain、Statistical Signal、Stealthy/Robust

figures.data_and_statistics: 概念流程图；不含样本、分母、聚合或不确定性。French/键示例是机制插图，不是测量值。
figures.evidence_relation: 引言的固定 query-key 失败 → Figure 1 的 domain trigger 与 distributed statistical signal → Sec. 3–4、Eq. (1)–(3)、Algorithm 1 → Tables 1–3 与 Figure 2 的实证。
design_strengths: 三 lane 并置把旧范式和新替换动作变成可追踪的视觉接口。
Threat Model、API、query/reply、check/X 同时用位置、文字和形状编码。
design_weaknesses: 小图标和浅色框在缩放或灰度下对比下降。
没有 query 数、检测阈值、成本或统计假设的量化边界。
figures.reusable_pattern: 先用威胁—旧方案—新方案的同画布概念图固定方法接口，再用结果图逐项填充新方案。

A lower recall indicates a stealthier fingerprint.

caption.text: Figure 3: Detectability Against Adversarial Paraphrasing We compare the detectability of our fingerprint (measured by the negative log p-value) with respect to the number of queries |Q| after paraphrasing and adversarial paraphrasing (Diaa et al., 2024). We generate the replies with LLAMA3.1-8B, and average all results over 5 independent runs. In red, we show the fingerprint decision threshold of 1e−03.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Ablation on the Watermark Strength Parameter (Left) We compare the detectability of our fingerprint (measured by the negative log p-value) with respect to the number of queries |Q| for different watermark strength parameters δ (Sec. 4.1). For both figures, we generate 1000 replies with QWEN2.5-3B fingerprinted on the French domain, and average the metrics over 5 independent runs.

encodings.shape: right circle markers; left colored curves
encodings.line: left solid curves + red dashed threshold; right solid line
encodings.text: δ legend, threshold, PPL axis and panel prose

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Figure 9: Ablation on Fingerprint Leakage We compare the detectability of our fingerprint (measured by the negative log p-value) with respect to the number of queries |Q| for different semantic domains. We see that only with the math domain is the fingerprint detected: there is no leakage.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Effectiveness of Our Fingerprint We compare the Fingerprint Success Rate (FSR) of 3 models with and without the fingerprint. We also compare utility, measured via benchmark accuracy, and report the average in the last column (AVG). We highlight in bold FSR values of 1.0. We highlight in blue the benchmark in French, as it uses the same semantic domain as our fingerprint.

tables.uncertainty: FSR is a 5-run mean of binary detector outcomes; no SD, interval or per-run values are shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: 3 models × Base/Fingerprinted; FSR uses one decimal, benchmark accuracies and AVG use two decimals; French benchmark column is blue.
tables.evidence_relation: Sec. 4 detector/FSR definition → Table 1 effectiveness and utility → Table 4/7 quality/domain slices and Table 8 regularizer ablation.
design_strengths: Base control, fingerprinted condition, FSR and utility share one decision surface.
Model groups and AVG make cross-model comparison compact.
design_weaknesses: Mixed metrics have no uncertainty or denominator display; wide 12-column layout compresses text.
The prose says 7 benchmarks while the table lists 8 benchmark columns.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use one stable model×condition table for detector outcome, utility, target-domain marker and average.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Robustness Evaluation Against Prominent Deployments We compare the Fingerprint Success Rate of LLAMA3.2-1B, QWEN2.5-3B and LLAMA3.1-8B models fingerprinted with either IF, SF or our fingerprint under various deployment scenarios. We highlight in green FSR of 1.0. Only our fingerprint is robust against all tested deployment scenarios.

tables.uncertainty: FSR is averaged over 5 independent binary detector runs; no interval or run-level variation.
tables.data_and_statistics: No Fingerprint plus 23 deployment rows; 12 semantic columns (3 modification hierarchy + 9 FSR method columns) and two narrow spacer columns; one decimal FSR.
tables.evidence_relation: Sec. 3 prior failure → Sec. 4 statistical signal → Table 2 prominent deployment matrix → Table 3 targeted adversaries and Table 5 complementary slices.
design_strengths: Hierarchical rows compress temperature, prompt, watermark, quantization, pruning, finetuning and active attacks.
Repeated model/method groups and green/pink cells make success/failure scanable.
design_weaknesses: 24 rows and 9 result columns make cells dense; color is the dominant success/failure cue.
Five-run aggregation hides detector instability and unlisted deployments.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed method/model matrix with hierarchical attack rows and low-saturation success/failure cells.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Robustness Evaluation Against Targeted Adversaries We compare the Fingerprint Success Rate of LLAMA3.2-1B, QWEN2.5-3B and LLAMA3.1-8B models fingerprinted with either IF, SF or our fingerprint against targeted adversaries particularly adversarial for our fingerprint. We highlight in green FSR of 1.0. Our fingerprint remains robust against all tested adversaries.

tables.uncertainty: FSR is averaged over 5 independent binary detector runs; no interval or run-level values.
tables.data_and_statistics: Five targeted rows: English prompt, WildChatFr LoRA/full, ADV paraphrasing and pre-filling; 12 semantic columns plus two spacer columns; one decimal FSR.
tables.evidence_relation: Targeted attack mechanism and query accumulation → Table 3 → Figure 3/6 curves and Table 2 prominent robustness.
design_strengths: Only the attacks most likely to remove the signal are isolated, while the model/method schema matches Table 2.
Green Ours cells and pink baseline failures are easy to align across models.
design_weaknesses: Targeted prompt/1000-query details live in Appendix A; colors and one-decimal FSR lack uncertainty.
The all-tested claim is bounded by five rows and three models.
tables.reusable_pattern: Split targeted adversaries into a small companion matrix instead of overloading the prominent-deployment table.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Additional Quality Metrics We study the impact on quality, measured through perplexity and GPT5-MINI-as-a-judge, and report the average across a thousand samples. The samples are generated on three different semantic domains: a general Q&A Domain, on Math questions and on French questions.

tables.uncertainty: Averages over 1000 samples; no dispersion or interval.
tables.data_and_statistics: 3 models × Base/Fingerprinted; General Q&A, Math and French each have PPL/GPT5 columns, all displayed to two decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 utility → Table 4 exposes domain-specific PPL/judge cost → Figure 8 δ trade-off and limitations.
design_strengths: Grouped two-metric/three-domain header is compact and model order matches Table 1.
Domain-specific quality cost is visible without changing model comparisons.
design_weaknesses: PPL and judge score directions are not indicated; 1000-sample average has no variability.
Perceived-quality drop requires reading across six metric columns.
tables.reusable_pattern: Append a domain×quality table after the main task-accuracy table, preserving model/condition order.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Complementary Robustness Evaluation We compare the Fingerprint Success Rate of LLAMA3.2-1B, QWEN2.5-3B and LLAMA3.1-8B models fingerprinted with either IF, SF or our fingerprint; after various modifications. We highlight in green FSR value of 1.0, as in Table 2.

tables.uncertainty: FSR is averaged over 5 independent binary detector runs; no interval.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four additional system prompts plus input/output Translation*; 12 semantic result columns and two narrow separators; one decimal FSR.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines the threat and replaces brittle query-key triggers with semantic-domain/statistical-signal components. Tables 1–3 then establish effectiveness, prominent robustness and targeted robustness; Figure 2 adds stealth. Appendix Tables 4–6 and Figures 3–9 expose quality, query accumulation, domain, strength, regularizer and leakage boundaries; Figures 10–12 test token, multi-key and harmful-domain extensions, and Table 9 closes the resource-cost boundary.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–8 use bold result-oriented titles followed by setup, comparison and threshold/aggregation details. Figures 10–12 and Table 9 are shorter; ROC captions omit several axis/sample/identity definitions. Five-run averaging is repeatedly stated for line plots, but the sole visible band in Figure 8 is not defined.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Utility tables reuse Model/Type-or-Domain, FSR, eight benchmark columns and AVG; robustness tables reuse hierarchical Modification plus three model groups and IF/SF/Ours. Quality groups metrics under General Q&A/Math/French; finetuneability uses Before/After task headers; cost uses one flat IF/Scalable/Ours header.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The semantic-domain and statistical-watermark mechanism in Eq. (1)–(3) is tested by FSR matrices, then unpacked through query-count, full-watermark, domain, δ, regularizer and leakage ablations. Figure 3/6 are the clearest mechanism-to-result bridge.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figure 1, Tables 1–3 and Figure 2 carry the headline decision; Appendix Tables 4–9 and Figures 3–12 provide quality cost, attack detail, query budget, leakage, theorem-adjacent extensions, multi-key/harmful boundaries and resources. Algorithm 1 and the D.1 proof are text/theory objects, not figure/table records.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Paper text and table/caption objects use Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern math at stable sizes; embedded chart assets introduce DejaVu Sans/ArialMT, and dense tables are resized. Figure 1 and Appendix G add diagram/card typography, so figure/table families are related but not identical.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Red dashed threshold and green/pink success semantics recur across plots/tables, while method/domain colors vary between Figure 2 and later curves. This is coherent within object families but not globally redundant or grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Use a page-width threat/prior/ours concept diagram to fix method interfaces before quantitative evidence.
Keep a stable FSR model×method matrix for prominent and targeted attacks, with hierarchical rows and explicit failure colors.
Plot detector power against log query count with a visible α threshold, and pair target-domain utility/leakage controls with the same detector story.
When multiple factors share a curve, reserve color for the primary role and use marker/line-style redundancy.
highest_value_objects: Table 2 and Table 3 for the bounded robustness evidence.
Figures 3 and 6 for the “weakened single-query signal → accumulated detection” mechanism.
Table 4 and Figure 9 for quality cost and domain-leakage boundaries.
failure_patterns: Large matrices and long legends are dense after resize; most curves have no dispersion display.
Figure 8’s band is not defined, and Figure 10–12 captions are too short to stand alone.
Color-only encodings weaken grayscale/accessibility; table rows preserve more redundant structure than curves.
Strong all-tested/no-leakage wording must remain bounded to listed models, attacks, domains, query budgets and domain-secrecy assumptions; the δ=4/5 and 7/8-benchmark inconsistencies remain visible.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Define semantic-domain triggering and diffused statistical evidence in one concept diagram, prove effectiveness/robustness/stealth with a repeated FSR matrix and log-query/ROC grammar, then use appendix quality, leakage, extension and cost objects to constrain the headline claims.
